title: Reconciler: refresh the integration branch from the base branch at run start (tracker records included)
description: Found by the Phase 1 gate run: after epic cia completed (run gate-cia-2), two follow-up ticks were created on ticks main; a new run (gate-cia-3) read its tracker from the integration branch epic/cia, where those ticks do not exist, and refused with 'epic cia has no dispatchable tick' although tk graph on main lists both as ready. The integration branch's tracker diverges from the base branch the moment either side writes, and today nothing folds the base back in. At run start (and on every restart), before planning, the reconciler must refresh the integration branch from the epic's base branch as origin has it: a merge of origin/<base> into origin/<integration> performed with ticks' own merge drivers for tracker records — the manifest's exit-code drivers merge-file (.tick/issues) and merge-activity (.tick/activity), declared in the target repo's .gitattributes — committed with plumbing and pushed with the store's CAS discipline; a source-file conflict is a typed refusal (resolve-conflict role, Phase 2), never a silent skip. Read the base branch from the epic tick (base_branch field via tk show --json) and fall back to the run's --base. Tests: a fixture where a tick is created on main after the run's first wave is dispatched on the next run; a fixture where main and the integration branch both wrote .tick/activity merges cleanly through merge-activity; a source conflict refuses. Scope: internal/reconcile (+ internal/tk if the merge drivers need a helper — merge-file/merge-activity are manifest commands). Runs after 0x1 (same package).
acceptance_criteria: A tick created on the base branch after the integration branch forked is planned and dispatched by the next run; tracker records from both sides merge via tk merge-file / merge-activity; a source conflict is refused with a typed reason; go test -short ./... green
